what_it_does: Millimeter-wave phased arrays (antenna systems that steer radio beams electronically) face a challenge: high-order wireless signals have high peak-to-average power ratios, and when the average power drops, efficiency plummets. Beamforming (steering the beam direction) and power back-off (reducing average power while maintaining peak) are typically handled separately in the baseband or RF domains. This paper unifies them: a spatial-temporal beamforming power amplifier integrates direct-digital amplitude-and-phase beamforming with power back-off into a single millimeter-wave amplifier architecture, then augments it with efficiency-boosting techniques like Doherty amplification or envelope tracking to restore efficiency even at reduced power levels.
